title: Upgrade to the latest 1.12 patch before leaving 1.12, or certificates may re-issue

detection.reason: the add-on version is resolved from the controller image tag to a MINOR; the hop axis is minors, so no rule can compare patch levels

quote: **IMPORTANT:** Before upgrading to any newer version, ensure you're running the latest v1.12 release. Otherwise, some certificates may be unexpectedly re-issued (see this comment).
remediation: Upgrade to the newest v1.12 patch release FIRST, then upgrade away from 1.12.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy -A -o json | jq -r '.items[].spec.template.spec.containers[] | select(.image | test("cert-manager-controller")) | .image'  # the patch component of this tag is what must be the newest 1.12 before upgrading

title: Feature gates set for the controller stop reaching the webhook at 1.13

detection.reason: checked in the webhook workload's container args only — a gate set through a config file or an environment variable is not scanned

quote: 1. If you deploy cert-manager using helm and have `.featureGates` value set, the features defined there will no longer be passed to cert-manager webhook, only to cert-manager controller. Use `webhook.featureGates` field instead to define features to be enabled on webhook. (https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/6093, https://github.com/irbekrm)
remediation: Move webhook feature gates to the `webhook.featureGates` Helm value. A controller-only gate passed to the webhook now fails startup unless the webhook has a feature by that name.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("webhook")) | .spec.template.spec.containers[].args[]? | select(test("feature-gates"))'  # each row is a gate list the 1.13 webhook validates against its OWN features

title: Known issue in 1.12–1.14: preferredChain may pick the wrong Let's Encrypt chain

detection.reason: `preferredChain` is not in the issuer projection

quote: ACME Issuer (Let's Encrypt): wrong certificate chain may be used if `preferredChain` is configured: see 1.14 release notes for more information.
remediation: If the target is one of these minors and an ACME issuer sets `preferredChain: ISRG Root X1`, either remove the field and renew, or accept the longer cross-signed chain while `DST Root CA X3` is trusted.
verifyCommand: kubectl get issuers,clusterissuers -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select((.spec.acme.preferredChain // "") != "") | "\(.kind)/\(.metadata.namespace // "cluster")/\(.metadata.name) preferredChain=\(.spec.acme.preferredChain)"'  # each row is an issuer the known issue can affect; NO rows = clean

title: The webhook rejects CertificateRequests whose CSR carries usages the resource does not declare

detection.reason: CertificateRequest objects and their CSR blobs are not collected; only tooling that builds its own CSRs is affected

quote: 3. Webhook validation of CertificateRequest resources is stricter now: all `KeyUsages` and `ExtendedKeyUsages` must be defined directly in the CertificateRequest resource, the encoded CSR can never contain more usages than defined in the Kubernetes resource. See `#6182` for more information.
remediation: Anything that creates CertificateRequests directly must list every KeyUsage and ExtendedKeyUsage of its CSR in `spec.usages`.
verifyCommand: kubectl get certificaterequests -A -o json --show-managed-fields | jq -r '.items[] | select([.metadata.managedFields[]?.manager] | map(select(test("cert-manager|cainjector") | not)) | .[0] != null) | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name) managers=\([.metadata.managedFields[].manager] | unique | join(","))"'  # each row was created by something other than cert-manager, whose CSRs the stricter check now applies to
